summary: Source-based expansion of the commutative and derived algebra behind deformation rings and patching. Coefficient categories C_Λ and Ĉ_Λ, small and essential surjections, fibre products and completed pushouts (Stacks Project ch. 90); Schlessinger's conditions, tangent spaces, versal and minimal versal objects, the Rim–Schlessinger condition, the automorphism-lifting criterion, lifts as torsors and Schlessinger's prorepresentability theorem (Stacks 90.10–90.19); the Galois-instance bound on presentation relations by dual Selmer groups (KW II Lemma 4.6) and the count of presentation variables (ACC+ Prop. 6.2.25); depth, the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula and dimension bounds (Stacks 10.72, 10.111; CG Lemma 6.1); characteristic-zero points from finiteness plus dimension and the finite-image finiteness criterion (KW II Cor. 4.7 and §§9–10; Khare–Wintenberger 2009 Lemma 3.6); patching of balanced modules (CG Prop. 2.3) and Kisin's patching criterion (Kisin 2009 Prop. 3.3.1, Lemma 3.3.4); freeness and near-faithfulness conclusions (CG Thm. 6.4); perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude and minimal models over local rings (Stacks 15.75–15.76); patched complexes with cohomology in a range of degrees (CG Thm. 6.3), ultrapatching (ACC+ §6.4), the codimension–amplitude lemma (CG Lemma 6.2), the derived length identity and the support theorem used to avoid Ihara's lemma (ACC+ §6.3). Imported Khare–Thorne and Gee–Newton lemmas, the Tor spectral sequence, Cohen–Macaulay/complete-intersection criteria and arithmetic inputs remain recorded gaps.

nodes.title: The Artinian coefficient category C_Λ, small extensions and fibre products
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a Noetherian ring and Λ → k a finite ring map to a field (classical case: Λ a complete Noetherian local ring such as a complete DVR O, k its residue field). C_Λ has objects pairs (A, φ) with A an Artinian local Λ-algebra and φ: A/m_A ≅ k a Λ-algebra isomorphism, and morphisms local Λ-algebra maps compatible with φ. A small extension is a surjection B → A whose kernel is a nonzero principal ideal annihilated by m_B; every surjection in C_Λ factors as a composition of small extensions. A map A → B in C_Λ is surjective iff m_A/m_A² → m_B/m_B² is, iff the map of relative cotangent spaces m_A/(m_Λ A + m_A²) → m_B/(m_Λ B + m_B²) is. A fibre product A₁ ×_A A₂ lies in C_Λ if one of the maps is surjective or k/k′ is separable (k′ = Λ/m_Λ), and if A₂ → A is a small extension so is A₁ ×_A A₂ → A₁; without these hypotheses the fibre product can fail to have residue field k. A surjection B → A is essential (any C → B with C → A surjective is itself surjective) iff B/(m_Λ B + m_B²) → A/(m_Λ A + m_A²) is an essential surjection; a further cotangent-space criterion under separability of k/k′ is Lemma 90.3.12, not read here.
hypotheses: Λ Noetherian, Λ → k finite with k a field; then m_Λ is maximal and k/k′ is finite.
Fibre products are only asserted in C_Λ under surjectivity of one map or separability of k/k′ (Example 90.3.7 gives a counterexample with k/k′ inseparable).
proofSteps: Factor B → A through B/I m_B^{n−1} → ⋯ → B/I and then through quotients by a k-basis of the kernel, which is a finite-dimensional k-vector space (Stacks Lemma 90.3.3).
Length over A equals length over Λ up to the factor [k : k′] (Lemma 90.3.4), so fibre products of Artinian rings are Artinian (Lemma 90.3.8 proof).
Surjectivity criterion: apply Nakayama's lemma twice using nilpotence of m_A (Lemma 90.3.5).
Residue field of A₁ ×_A A₂: surjectivity of one projection, or Hensel lifting of a primitive element when k/k′ is separable (Lemma 90.3.8).
acceptance: O[[X₁, …, X_d]]/m^n and k[ε] = k[x]/(x²) are objects; k[V] = k ⊕ V for finite-dimensional V is an object.
Example 90.3.7: Λ = F_p(t₁,…,t_n), k = F_p(x₁,…,x_n), t_i ↦ x_i^p, with two maps k → k[ε] whose fibre product is not in C_Λ.
Keep the residue-field identification φ as data when Λ → k is not surjective.

nodes.title: The complete Noetherian local category Ĉ_Λ: limits, completed pushouts and cotangent finiteness
nodes.statement: Ĉ_Λ has objects Noetherian complete local Λ-algebras R with an identification R/m_R ≅ k and local Λ-algebra maps; C_Λ ⊂ Ĉ_Λ is the full subcategory of Artinian objects and every R equals lim_n R/m_R^n with Artinian terms. A map in Ĉ_Λ is surjective iff it is surjective on m/m² (or on relative cotangent spaces). Ĉ_Λ has pushouts, given by the m-adic completion of S₁ ⊗_R S₂ (a Noetherian complete local ring with residue field k), and coproducts of pairs via the completion of R ⊗_Λ S. For S in Ĉ_Λ, dim_k Der_Λ(S, k) < ∞; if Der_Λ(S, k) → Der_Λ(R, k) is injective then R → S is surjective. An inverse system … → A₃ → A₂ → A₁ of surjections in C_Λ with bounded dim_k(m_{A_n}/m²_{A_n}) has limit S in Ĉ_Λ, and the kernels of S → A_n define the m_S-adic topology; its proof uses the auxiliary Lemma 90.4.7: a decreasing sequence of ideals J_n ⊃ m^n with intersection J defines the adic topology on R/J.
hypotheses: Λ Noetherian, Λ → k finite; completed tensor products are taken in Ĉ_Λ, i.e. over an object R of Ĉ_Λ or over Λ with the kernel of the multiplication map to k.
An initial object of Ĉ_Λ exists in the classical case (Λ itself) and when k/k′ is separable, but not when k/k′ is inseparable.
proofSteps: Surjectivity: equality of relative cotangent spaces of R and R/m^n for n ≥ 2 and Lemma 90.3.5 give surjectivity at each finite level; the kernels form a Mittag-Leffler system of Artinian modules, so the limit is surjective (Stacks Lemma 90.4.2).

Pushouts and coproducts: the tensor product has a finitely generated maximal ideal with residue field k; its completion is Noetherian complete local (Algebra, Lemma 10.97.5); the universal property is stated with details omitted (Lemmas 90.4.3–90.4.4).

Der_Λ(S, k) is bounded by the number of generators of the relative cotangent space plus generators of k over k′ via the Leibniz rule (Lemma 90.4.5); injectivity on derivations gives surjectivity through the quotient derivation S → S/(f(R) + m_R S + m_S²) (Lemma 90.4.6).
Limits: choose generators of m_{A_n} lifting to S, map a completed polynomial ring over Λ onto the system, and use Krull's intersection theorem to identify the topology (Lemmas 90.4.7–90.4.8).
acceptance: O[[X₁,…,X_d]] is an object with relative cotangent space of dimension d over Λ = O; record relative and absolute dimensions separately (roadmap convention).
The completed tensor product of two quotients of power series rings over O is again Noetherian local; do not assert this for non-local or non-Noetherian inputs.
Framing variables add power-series variables; keep the framed ring distinct from the unframed one.

nodes.title: Schlessinger's conditions (S1), (S2) and tangent spaces
nodes.statement: For a category F cofibred in groupoids over C_Λ (in particular a functor F: C_Λ → Sets), (S1) requires that for A₁ → A and a surjection A₂ → A every compatible pair of objects over A₁, A₂ comes from an object over A₁ ×_A A₂ (for functors: F(A₁ ×_A A₂) → F(A₁) ×_{F(A)} F(A₂) surjective, Schlessinger's (H1)); it suffices to check small extensions. (S2) requires the same for A → k and k[ε] → k and, moreover, that two such completions y, y′ over A ×_k k[ε] with maps a: y → x, a′: y′ → x admit b: y → y′ with a = a′ ∘ b (for functors: bijectivity, Schlessinger's (H2)); (S2) then holds with k[ε] replaced by k[V] for any finite-dimensional V. The tangent space is T F = F(k[ε]) (isomorphism classes for predeformation categories); under (S2) (for the functor of isomorphism classes) it is a k-vector space with F(k[V]) = T F ⊗_k V. For a prorepresentable F = Hom(S, −), T F = Der_Λ(S, k), finite-dimensional, and in the classical case equal to the dual of the relative cotangent space.
hypotheses: F cofibred in groupoids over C_Λ; a predeformation category has F(k) equivalent to a point.

(S2) passes to the functor of isomorphism classes provided one of the sufficient conditions of Lemma 90.10.5(2) holds: F a predeformation category, F(k) a set or setoid, or Aut_{k[ε]}(x_ε) → Aut_k(x₀) surjective for all x_ε → x₀ over k[ε] → k.
proofSteps: (S1) says the functor F(A₁ ×_A A₂) → F(A₁) ×_{F(A)} F(A₂) of (90.10.1.1) is essentially surjective; the second part of (S2) implies that two objects which become isomorphic in the target are isomorphic in the source, but the source notes it is not equivalent to this.
Reduction of (S1) to small extensions uses Lemma 90.3.3 by induction; the source omits the proof ('Proof omitted. Hints', Lemma 90.10.2).
(S2) for k[V] by induction on dim V via k[V] = k[V′] ×_k k[ε] (Lemma 90.10.4, proof given).

A functor preserving finite products and sending 0 to a point has a unique linear structure (Lemmas 90.11.4–90.11.8; the module verification in 90.11.4 and the proof of 90.11.5 are omitted in the source); apply to M ↦ F(k[M]) (Lemma 90.12.2).
For prorepresentable functors Hom(S, k[V]) = Der_Λ(S, V), finite-dimensional by Lemma 90.4.5 (Example 90.11.11).
acceptance: Condition dim_k T F < ∞ is Schlessinger's (H3) (Remark 90.13.5).

Example 90.15.3: from a finite nontrivial subgroup G ⊂ Aut_{C_Λ}(k[ε]) the source builds F with a versal formal object satisfying (90.15.0.2) but failing (S2), so (2) does not imply (3) in Theorem 90.15.5.

Framed deformation functors satisfy (RS) and hence (S1)–(S2). Unframed strict-equivalence functors are isomorphism classes of a predeformation category with (RS), so they still satisfy (S1)–(S2) (Lemmas 90.16.6, 90.10.5); when automorphisms do not lift they fail (RS)/(H4) (Lemma 90.16.7).

nodes.title: Versal and minimal versal formal objects; existence of hulls
nodes.statement: For a predeformation category F: (S1) + (S2) + dim_k T F < ∞ imply the existence of a versal formal object; if a versal formal object exists then a minimal versal formal object exists, minimal versal objects are unique up to (non-canonical) isomorphism, and every versal object is the pushforward of a minimal one along a power-series extension R = R′[[x₁,…,x_r]]. Theorem 90.15.5: for the conditions (1) a minimal versal object with dξ: Der_Λ(R, k) → T F bijective, (2) a minimal versal object with dξ bijective on Der_Λ(k, k)-orbits, (3) (S1), (S2), dim T F < ∞, one has (1) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (2), and all are equivalent if k/k′ is separable. In the classical case this recovers Schlessinger's hull: a versal object inducing an isomorphism on tangent spaces exists under (H1)–(H3). A hull need not prorepresent F.
hypotheses: F a predeformation category over C_Λ; the separability of k/k′ is needed to identify (1) and (2).
Versality and smoothness of morphisms of categories cofibred in groupoids (§90.8) are used as defined there (not re-read).
proofSteps: Existence of a versal object (Lemma 90.13.4) builds ideals J_n ⊂ S = R[[X₁,…,X_r]] minimal with liftability, using smoothness of R|C_Λ and (S1) at each step; only the final step of this proof was read (p. 6547).
Minimal objects in the categories S_x of sub-objects over subrings exist by finite length; (S1) makes minimality compatible with pushforward and surjections (Lemma 90.14.1).

Lemma 90.14.2 builds a compatible minimal sub-object ξ′ over R′ = lim R′_n ⊂ R, Noetherian by versality and Lemma 90.4.8; Lemma 90.14.3 shows R ≅ R′[[x₁,…,x_r]] and ξ′ versal, using the section property and Lemma 90.4.9.
Uniqueness: maps between minimal versal objects are surjective both ways, hence isomorphisms (Lemma 90.14.5).

Lemma 90.15.4: under (S2) a minimal versal object satisfies (90.15.0.2); otherwise a nonzero D ∈ Ker(dξ) not vanishing on m_R/m_R² gives R′ = {a ∈ R : D(a) = 0}, contradicting Lemma 90.14.2(1). Lemma 90.15.2 gives (1) ⇒ (3).

For F = C_Λ itself the minimal versal ring is the formally smooth R of Lemma 90.9.5 (Example 90.15.8).
The power-series ambiguity R = R′[[x]] is the framing/auxiliary-variable phenomenon; track the number of variables.

nodes.title: Rim–Schlessinger condition, automorphism lifting and Schlessinger's prorepresentability theorem
nodes.statement: (RS) requires that fibre products x₁ ×_x x₂ exist over A₁ ×_A A₂ whenever A₂ → A is surjective; equivalently F(A₁ ×_A A₂) → F(A₁) ×_{F(A)} F(A₂) is an equivalence (it suffices to check small extensions); for functors this is Schlessinger's (H4). (RS) implies (S1) and (S2). If F satisfies (RS), the functor of isomorphism classes F̄ satisfies (RS) iff for every x′ → x over a surjection (equivalently a small extension) A′ → A the map Aut_{A′}(x′) → Aut_A(x) is surjective. For a deformation category and a surjection A′ → A with kernel I annihilated by m_{A′}, the set of lifts of x, when nonempty, is a torsor under T F ⊗_k I; infinitesimal automorphisms Inf(x′/x) form a torsor under Inf_{x₀}(F) ⊗_k I. Schlessinger's theorem: F: C_Λ → Sets is prorepresentable iff F is a deformation functor (F(k) a point and (RS)), dim_k T F < ∞, and Der_Λ(k, k) → T F is injective; a smooth morphism of deformation functors inducing an isomorphism on tangent spaces is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: F cofibred in groupoids over C_Λ; condition (c) on Der_Λ(k, k) is empty when k/k′ is separable.
Unframed deformation functors whose objects have automorphisms that do not lift along small extensions are not prorepresentable, even when a hull exists.
proofSteps: (RS) ⇔ equivalence of fibre categories via the 2-fibre product description (Stacks Lemma 90.16.4); (RS) ⇒ (S1), (S2) (Lemma 90.16.6).
Automorphism criterion: compare F(A₁) ×_{F(A)} F(A₂) with its isomorphism classes; injectivity is equivalent to lifting automorphisms (Lemma 90.16.7, proof given).
Lifts torsor: identify A′ ×_A A′ ≅ A′ ×_k k[I] and use (RS) bijections to define a free transitive action of Lift(x₀, k[I]) = T F ⊗ I (Lemma 90.17.5).
Lemma 90.18.1: induct on length through small extensions; smoothness gives surjectivity and the torsor structures give bijectivity on fibres.

Theorem 90.18.2: prorepresentable ⇒ (RS), finite tangent space, injectivity; conversely take a minimal versal ξ over R with (90.15.0.2) (Theorem 90.15.5), which is bijective on T by (c), so ξ: R|C_Λ → F is an isomorphism by Lemma 90.18.1.
acceptance: Framed deformation functors of a residual representation are prorepresentable once dim_k T F < ∞ (Theorem 90.18.2(b); e.g. under a finiteness condition on the group); unframed ones need in addition that automorphisms lift, e.g. when the centralizer consists of scalars.
Infinitesimal automorphisms: addition in Inf_{x₀}(F) agrees with composition (Lemma 90.19.9).
Do not identify a hull with a representing ring when Lemma 90.16.7(3) fails (roadmap requirement).

nodes.title: Presentations over local deformation rings and the bound on relations (Galois instance)
nodes.statement: For a global deformation problem with local deformation rings, there is a presentation R_{S,ψ}^□ ≅ R_{S,loc,ψ}[[X₁,…,X_g]]/J inducing an isomorphism on tangent spaces relative to R_{S,loc,ψ}, with g computed by the Galois cohomology complex (ACC+ Prop. 6.2.25 computes only this number of variables, g = h¹_{S,T}(ad ρ̄)), and the minimal number of generators of J satisfies r(J) = dim J/mJ ≤ dim H¹_{L⊥}(S, (Ad⁰)*(1)) (KW II Lemma 4.6; ACC+ gives no relation bound). Consequently the absolute dimension of the global ring is bounded below by that of the local ring plus the excess of variables over relations; for KW II this gives abs.dim R̄_S^ψ ≥ 1.
hypotheses: Absolutely irreducible residual representation with the local conditions of each source. KW II treats all p (with the correction term δ_p, δ_p = 0 for p > 2 and δ₂ = 1) and fixes the determinant ψ; ACC+ does not fix the determinant (ad ρ̄ = M_n(k)), assumes p ∤ 2n throughout, and in Proposition 6.2.25 takes T ⊆ S nonempty with Λ_v = O for v ∈ S∖T.

The Galois inputs are arithmetic suppliers, not commutative algebra: KW II uses Wiles' formula (Proposition 4.5) and Poitou–Tate duality (Lemma 4.6, via NSW 8.6.7–8.6.8); ACC+ uses the local and global Euler characteristic formulas, part of the Poitou–Tate sequence and local Tate duality.
proofSteps: Relative tangent space: T-framed lifts to k[ε] trivial at v ∈ T and of type S correspond to 1-cocycles of the complex C•_{S,T}(ad ρ̄), and strict equivalence to coboundaries, giving H¹_{S,T} ≅ Hom(R_S^T/m_{R^{T,loc}}, k[ε]) (ACC+ Prop. 6.2.25 proof).

Hence a surjection R^{T,loc}_S[[X₁,…,X_g]] → R_S^T with g = h¹_{S,T}(ad ρ̄); since T ≠ ∅, h⁰_{S,T} = 0, and g is computed from (6.2.24) with the local and global Euler characteristic formulas and part of the Poitou–Tate sequence.

(Commutative-algebra step) For nonzero u ∈ Hom(J/mJ, k) push the extension 0 → J/mJ → P/mJ → R → 0 along u to 0 → I_u → R_u → R → 0 with I_u ≅ k, I_u² = 0; a section of R_u → R over the local ring would induce an isomorphism on relative tangent spaces, hence be an isomorphism, which is impossible (KW II Lemma 4.6 proof).

(Arithmetic step) The obstruction to lifting the tautological point to R_u defines a pairing with H¹_{L⊥}(S, (Ad⁰)*(1)) through a 2-cocycle, local cochains and Poitou–Tate; injectivity of u ↦ f(u) follows (KW II Lemma 4.6).

Dimension bound: abs.dim R̄_{S,ψ} ≥ |S| − 1 + abs.dim R̄_{S,loc,ψ} = 4|S| (using abs.dim R̄_{S,loc,ψ} = 1 + 3|S|); comparison with abs.dim R̄_S^ψ + 4|S| − 1 gives abs.dim R̄_S^ψ ≥ 1 (Proposition 4.5).
acceptance: If the local rings are Cohen–Macaulay and R̄_S^ψ is finite over O, the elements y₁,…,y_{4|S|−1}, r₁,…,r_{r(J)}, p form a regular sequence and R̄_S^ψ is flat, CM or a complete intersection accordingly (KW II, Remarks after the proof of Proposition 4.5, p. 45).
Keep framed and unframed rings distinct: framing adds power-series variables.

nodes.title: Depth, the Auslander–Buchsbaum formula and dimension bounds for finite modules
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian local ring (R, m) and nonzero finite module M: depth(M) (the maximal length of an M-regular sequence in m) is the least i with Ext^i_R(R/m, M) ≠ 0; dim Supp(M) ≥ depth(M); depth behaves along short exact sequences by the three inequalities of Lemma 10.72.6; for x ∈ m regular on M, depth(M/xM) = depth(M) − 1 and regular sequences extend to length depth(M). If M has finite projective dimension then depth(R) = pd_R(M) + depth(M) (Auslander–Buchsbaum). If N has depth n and 0 ≠ M ⊆ N then dim M ≥ n (via depth ≤ min_{p ∈ Ass} dim R/p). A Noetherian local ring is regular iff it has finite global dimension, and then all localizations are regular. For a map A → D of Noetherian domains of the same finite dimension and a nonzero D-module L finite projective over A, A → D is finite; if A and D are regular, L is finite projective and faithful over D.
hypotheses: Noetherian local rings and finite modules; Auslander–Buchsbaum needs finite projective dimension.
The inequality depth(M) ≤ dim R/p for p ∈ Ass(M) is Stacks Algebra Lemma 10.72.9 (tag 0BK4); Calegari–Geraghty cite it from Matsumura Theorem 17.2.
proofSteps: Ext characterization by induction on depth using the long exact Ext sequence of 0 → M → M → M/xM → 0, where multiplication by x ∈ m acts by zero on Ext(κ, −) (Stacks Lemma 10.72.5).

nodes.title: Characteristic-zero points of a finite O-algebra of positive dimension
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field k that is finite as an O-module (equivalently as a Z_p-module, O being finite over Z_p) and has Krull dimension ≥ 1. Then p is not nilpotent in R, there is a prime I with p ∉ I, and R → R/I ↪ O′ gives a local O-algebra map to the ring of integers O′ of a finite extension of Frac(O). The dimension hypothesis cannot be dropped: a nonzero finite O-algebra such as k has no characteristic-zero point. If R^□ is formally smooth over R, points of R lift to R^□ after a further finite extension.
hypotheses: R finite over O and abs.dim R ≥ 1 (in KW II the dimension bound comes from the presentation node).

R/I is a domain finite over O in which p ≠ 0, so its fraction field E′ is a finite extension of Frac(O) and R/I lies in the ring of integers O′ of E′ (finite, hence integral).
The composite R → R/I ⊂ O′ is the required point; for the framed ring use formal smoothness of R̄_{S,ψ}^□ over R̄_S^ψ.

nodes.title: Finiteness criteria: finite image of the universal representation and finiteness after patching
nodes.statement: (Khare–Wintenberger) Let κ be a finite field of characteristic p, G a profinite group satisfying Mazur's p-finiteness condition, η: G → GL_N(κ) absolutely irreducible, F_N(κ) a subcategory of deformations of η in κ-algebras satisfying the conditions of Mazur §23, and η_F: G → GL_N(R_F) its universal deformation. Then R_F is finite (as a set) iff η_F(G) is finite. Used mod p: a deformation ring R is finite over Z_p iff R/(p) is finite, and the lemma is applied to the universal representation reduced mod p. (KW II §9.1, p = 2 case, Proposition 9.3) Once M_∞ is a faithful R_∞-module (Lemma 9.6(b)) and finite over O[[y₁,…,y_{h+j}]], R_∞ injects into End_{O[[y]]}(M_∞), which is finite over O[[y]], so R_∞ is finite over O[[y₁,…,y_{h+j}]], the framed ring R̄_{S,ψ} = R_∞/(y₁,…,y_h) is finite over O[[y_{h+1},…,y_{h+j}]] (framing variables), and the unframed R̄_S^ψ = R_∞/(y₁,…,y_{h+j}) is finite over O.

nodes.title: Perfect complexes, Tor-amplitude and minimal complexes over local rings
nodes.statement: An object K of D(R) is perfect if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective R-modules; equivalently K is pseudo-coherent of finite Tor dimension, and if K has Tor-amplitude in [a, b] it is represented by finite projectives in degrees [a, b]. Perfect objects satisfy two-out-of-three in triangles and are closed under summands; a bounded complex with perfect cohomology is perfect. Projective amplitude in [a, b] means quasi-isomorphism to projectives in degrees [a, b]. Over a local ring (R, m, κ), a pseudo-coherent K is represented by a complex with terms R^{d_i}, d_i = dim_κ H^i(K ⊗^L κ), unique up to isomorphism (minimal complex); two bounded finite projective representatives of the same perfect object become isomorphic after adding trivial complexes locally. Consequently for perfect K over a local ring, K ⊗^L κ = 0 implies K = 0, and the ranks of a minimal complex are determined by K ⊗^L κ. Three amplitudes must be distinguished: the degrees of a chosen complex, the Tor-amplitude, and the degrees of nonzero cohomology.
hypotheses: R commutative; for minimal complexes R local and K pseudo-coherent.
Derived completeness hypotheses are needed for Nakayama-type statements for non-pseudo-coherent complexes (supplied by DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, Stacks 15.92.19–15.92.20).
proofSteps: Perfect ⇔ pseudo-coherent + finite Tor dimension: represent by finite free terms bounded above, truncate at the lower Tor bound; the truncated term is finitely presented and flat, hence finite projective (Stacks Lemma 15.75.2).

Two-out-of-three and summands combine Lemma 15.75.2 with the corresponding statements for pseudo-coherence and Tor amplitude (Lemmas 15.75.4–15.75.5, citing 15.65.6 and 15.67.5); the statements on bounded complexes with perfect cohomology use truncations (Lemmas 15.75.6–15.75.7).

nodes.title: Codimension of support versus amplitude of a perfect complex over a regular local ring
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension n ≥ l₀ and P a perfect complex of S-modules concentrated in degrees 0,…,l₀. Then codim H*(P) ≤ l₀. If equality holds, P is a projective resolution of H^{l₀}(P), H^{l₀}(P) has depth n − l₀ and projective dimension l₀, and H^i(P) = 0 for i < l₀.
hypotheses: S regular local (finite global dimension, so Auslander–Buchsbaum applies to all finite modules); P perfect in the stated degree range.
The case l₀ = 1 is the length-one resolution situation of Proposition 2.3; l₀ = 0 is the classical setting (Diamond's Theorem 2.1, as cited by Calegari–Geraghty).
proofSteps: Let m ≤ l₀ be minimal with H^m(P) ≠ 0; the truncation P⁰ → ⋯ → P^m is a projective resolution of K^m = P^m/Im δ^{m−1}, so pd K^m ≤ m (CG Lemma 6.2 proof).
H^m(P) ⊆ K^m, so codim H^m(P) = n − dim H^m(P) ≤ n − depth K^m = pd K^m ≤ m, using CG Lemma 6.1 and Auslander–Buchsbaum.
If codim H*(P) ≥ l₀ then m = l₀, codim H^{l₀}(P) = l₀, P resolves H^{l₀}(P) and pd = l₀, hence depth = n − l₀.
acceptance: The Koszul complex of a regular sequence of length l₀ in S attains equality.
[O —p→ O] over S = O (n = 1, l₀ = 1): cohomology O/p of codimension 1 in the top degree, zero after inverting p.
Characteristic-zero concentration of cohomology in [q₀, q₀ + l₀] does not imply vanishing of torsion cohomology outside these degrees (roadmap warning).

nodes.title: Length identity for derived reduction modulo a nonzerodivisor
nodes.statement: (Modules) Let T be an excellent local ring with Spec T irreducible, f ∈ m_T and T/(f) of dimension 0. If dim T = 0 then lg_T(M/fM) − lg_T(M[f]) = 0 for all finite M; otherwise dim T = 1 with a unique non-maximal prime p and there is a ∈ Z_{>0} with lg_T(M/fM) − lg_T(M[f]) = a·lg_{T_p}(M_p) for all finite M. (Idempotent localization) If A is Noetherian and m is a maximal ideal that is a minimal prime, then A ≅ A_m × B. For S Noetherian, T a finite S-algebra acting on C ∈ D^b(S) through T → End_{D^b(S)}(C), and p a minimal prime of T over q ⊂ S, set C_p = e_p(C ⊗ S_q) with e_p the idempotent of T_q = T_p × B; this is not literally a localization over T. (Derived) If S is excellent local, f ∈ m_S a nonzerodivisor, T finite over S with maximal m such that Spec T_m is irreducible and T_m/(f) has dimension 0, then for every C with finitely generated cohomology and T-action, lg_{T_m}((C ⊗^L_S S/(f))_m) = 0 if dim T_m = 0 and = a·lg_{T_p}(C_p) otherwise, where lg_T(C) = Σ(−1)^i lg_T(H^i(C)) is additive in exact triangles with compatible T-actions when two of the three complexes have cohomology of finite length over T.
hypotheses: Excellence (to make the normalization of T/p finite); f a nonzerodivisor on S in the derived statement; T acts only through End in D^b(S), no strict chain model.
For perfect C the finiteness hypotheses are automatic and a subalgebra T of End is finite over S.
proofSteps: Dimension 0: T Artinian; the identity is additive in short exact sequences (snake lemma) and holds for T/m (ACC+ Lemma 6.3.2 proof).

Dimension 1: take a = lg_T(T̃/(f)) for the normalization T̃ of T/p, finite by excellence; the identity holds for T/m and for T̃, and is two-out-of-three; filter M by p^iM to reduce to T/p-modules, then to T̃-modules using the exact sequence with Tor₁(M, T̃/(T/p)) and M ⊗ T̃/(T/p) of finite length, and conclude by the structure theorem over the semilocal PID T̃.
Lemma 6.3.3: lift the idempotent of A/(m ∩ I) ≅ A/m × A/I, I the intersection of other minimal primes, through the nilpotent m ∩ I.
Lemma 6.3.4: both sides are additive in exact triangles with T-action; reduce to C ≅ M[i], where C ⊗^L S/(f) ≅ (M —f→ M)[−i], and apply Lemma 6.3.2 to T_m.
acceptance: Test on T = O, f = ϖ: a = 1 and lg(M/ϖM) − lg(M[ϖ]) = rank of M.
Check that the derived length is computed with the idempotent C_p and not with a nonexistent T-module localization.

Assume dim R_∞ = dim R′_∞ = dim S_∞ − l₀ and dim R_∞/ϖ = dim R′_∞/ϖ = dim S_∞ − l₀ − 1; generic points of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞ and Spec R_∞/ϖ not of maximal dimension have dimension < dim S_∞ − l₀ − 1; each top-dimensional generic point of Spec R_∞/ϖ specializes from a unique top-dimensional generic point of Spec R_∞, Spec R′_∞ has a unique top-dimensional generic point; and there is a one-dimensional characteristic-zero prime p ⊃ a_∞ of S_∞ with H*(C_∞ ⊗^L S_∞/p)[1/p] ≠ 0 concentrated in [q₀, q₀ + l₀]. Theorem 90.18.2 reads 'Let F : C_Lambda -> Sets be a functor. Then F is prorepresentable if and only if (a) F is a deformation functor, (b) dim_k T F is finite, and (c) gamma : Der_Lambda(k,k) -> T F is injective', so the node's excerpt and its three conditions are exact; the book's own note that condition (c) is empty when k'/k is separable is recorded in the node's hypotheses. Lemma 90.16.7's automorphism-lifting criterion and the lifts torsor of Lemma 90.17.5 also match.
